about: The epistola of the formulary “Sunday after Ascension” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Dearly beloved: Be prudent and watch in prayers. But before all things have a constant mutual charity among yourselves, for charity covers a multitude of sins. Be hospitable to one another without murmuring. As each one has received grace, minister it to one another as good stewards of the manifold grace of God. If anyone speaks, let him speak as the words of God; if anyone ministers, let him do it as from the power which God supplies, that in all things God may be honored through Jesus Christ our Lord.

ex.w016: The participle describes the faithful Peter addresses: they are to keep a mutual and constant charity. The sentence has no verb in the second person, and no separate word expresses its subject, an understood you.
ex.w022: The adjective is the predicate of an understood subject, the faithful Peter addresses. The Latin leaves out both the subject and the verb: “[be] hospitable to one another”.
ex.w033: The plural participle describes the faithful, although the singular “unusquísque” comes before it: each is to minister to the others the grace received. No separate word expresses its subject.
